articleTitle: Process Integration of Unique Identification Marks Using Inkjet Technologies for Backside Coating Tape
abstract: Semiconductors are used in many of the electronic devices for our daily lives, such as smartphones and personal computers, but counterfeit semiconductor packages have been increasing in recent years. Determination of authenticity in hardware as one of the measures has been required due to this trend. To prevent semiconductor counterfeiting, it is common to use laser marking to make logos, serial numbers, and other identifiers. In this case, X-ray or electrical response need to be used to determine whether the product is counterfeit or not. However, such methods are costly, making it difficult to analyze all semiconductor products. We propose an anti-counterfeiting solution which utilize unique identification mark with fine randomness in the ink impact minute droplet while printing. This method allows for the simple identification of counterfeit and also reduces costs compared to conventional methods, making it suitable for determining the authenticity of semiconductor products. In this study, we investigated the optimal process suitability for the construction of this technology. We prepared two kinds of backside coating tapes and two printing process; 1) printing before heat cured of backside coating tape, 2) printing after heat cured of backside coting tape. As a result, the samples of four conditions can be used as identifiable ID. On the other hand, no delamination happens to the printing before heat cured condition regardless of kinds of backside coating tapes. The test results indicate that the process printing before heat cured is the optimal process.

articleTitle: Study of Solder Ball Hardness on Wafer Level Chip Size Packages
abstract: There are some challenges in electronic industries to achieve robustness in Thermal Cycling performance on board for big Wafer Level Chip Size Packages (WLCSP), though usually no concern or robust in Drop Test reliability, partly WLCSP is typically less ball counts and much smaller package size compared to Ball-Grid-Array (BGA). It is essential to balance the solder joint hardness for the overall robustness in the field application where the WLCSP could be subjected various loading conditions like Thermal Cycling Test on Board (TCoB), Bend, Drop etc. In this paper, solder joint hardness was studied for different solder alloy Sn-Ag-Cu of WLCSPs on PCB board before and after thermal cycling test (e.g. 1000 cycles) to improve the TC on Board performance. Berkovich micro indentation technique was used and optimized for providing precise and consistent measurements of indentation hardness. The experimental results showed that hardness of solder alloy induced by Ag or different % in Bi, solder paste, faster cooling after reflowing, softening during annealing and deterioration during TC, which may eventually affect the TCoB performance. Hardness could be a good, simple, and cost-effective indicator for solder joint reliability. It can be used for alloy selection, reflow profile optimization, and investigating aging impact etc.

articleTitle: Leadframe Strip Stiffness Simulation for Identification of Issues During Package Singulation Process
abstract: Electronic assembly processes of the leadframe strip with high density package designs regularly deal with significant strip warpage after the Post Mold Cure (PMC) process. The Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE) mismatch of the Epoxy Mold Compound to the leadframe and chip causes the strip to warp. This will affect the succeeding assembly process which is package singulation. To ensure that the leadframe strip is flat for singulation process, a certain amount of vacuum pressure is applied to the leadframe strip. One of the root causes that resulted in vacuum process failure is the stiffness of the leadframe strip. This paper deals with Quad-Flat No-lead package (QFN) strip modelling using a Finite Element Analysis (FEA) approach to understand the contributing factors to the stiffness of the strip. To validate the model, the leadframe strip stiffness is measured using a Three-Point Bending (3PB) test. The effect of Silicon (Si) die content to the strip stiffness was analyzed. The accuracy of the model is ensured by validating the simulation results with the experimental data. The deviation of both results is less than 10% for all simulated cases. The simulation trends show that higher die to die pad ratio for equivalent package size leads to higher strip stiffness which result in a harder to flatten the strip during the vacuum mount process. The simulated trend agrees with the actual observation. However, the dependence of the strip stiffness on die-to-die pad ratio is quite weak, as reducing the die-to-die pad ratio from 90% to 60% will decrease the strip stiffness about 3%. The validated model enables the authors to explore more on other factors of the leadframe stiffness for instance, different Bill of Materials (BOM) and other geometrical variations.

articleTitle: Improvement of Laser Groove Bottom Width in Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) Low-k Wafer Technology
abstract: This paper describes the development work of controlling the U-shape profiler during laser grooving in Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) low-k wafer technology. The effects of laser parameter, i.e. laser power frequency and feed speed were investigated. The sample dies were thoroughly examined and characterized, which included assessing the grooving quality, shape, and profile. The design of experiment (DOE) methodology was applied to understand parameter correlations and to statistically predict the optimum parameters. Subsequently, the parameters were fine-tuned to ensure that they fell within the acceptable limits for the production environment. In this study, various inspection tools and methods were utilized, including a 3D profiler high-power microscope, scanning electron microscope (SEM), and focused ion beam (FIB). Differential interference contrast (DIC) light was also employed to detect inter metal dielectric (IMD) layer cracks, which was crucial in distinguishing failures associated with the laser process or combination effects due to additional stress during mechanical sawing. This study provides significant benefits to the field of laser processing and CMOS low-k technology by improving product quality, establishing a robust process for the production line, enhancing knowledge and expertise in the field.

articleTitle: Overshoot concerns for fixed voltage rails with high layout resistance (Rpath) in advanced SoCs
abstract: New features and Intellectual Property (IP) are constantly added into Advanced SoCs. These features result in the increase of max current (ICCmax) demands of the platform, primarily impacting voltage regulators (VR) requirements. Previously only compute power rails consumed high current, but now even the peripheral rails within the same SoC can consume 40A or more. Compute rails are typically able to change their voltages (VID) along with circuitry that can operate at wide voltage ranges. Peripheral rails do not have this feature and will only work with fixed voltages and tolerances. To meet minimum voltage (Vmin) requirements, remote sensing is often used where the sense is placed at the load. This paper explains why this has negative consequences and how it is related to the layout path resistance (Rpath) and the voltage difference between VR output and sense. Voltage regulators can compensate for droop but are mostly bystanders for overshoot, relying only on platform component parameters such as inductance, resistance, and capacitance to mitigate. Calculations and simulation results are shown to demonstrate the behavior. It concludes with the solution space involving layout and VR features to mitigate it as well as how this can be done in early stage SoC development period to avoid future issues.

articleTitle: Wave Solder Process characterization in PCBA
abstract: Electronics products are integrated part of our daily lives. Given examples of electronics components which will be assembled onto a Printed Circuit Board (PCB) for enabling of AI application in all aspect of human daily life, example in automobile for self-driving, E-Commerce, education etc. In order to manufacture an electronic product, two types of assembly technologies used in PCBA industry namely Surface Mount Technology (SMT) and Thru-Hole Technology (THT). SMT can be applied to very small size and high signal counts components on Small Mount Device (SMD) which does not require strong mechanical interconnection. where components are placed automatically by SMT placement machine to the PCB top or bottom surfaces with SMT solder paste then goes through SMT reflow process to form mechanical and electrical interconnections. On the other hand, THT is applied for Pin- Through Hole (PTH) components which insert through holes component leads into the drill-holes of PCB. Then the end of the leads on bottom side of PCB will be spray with wave solder flux, follow by passing through a bath of molten solder, with this process is called as wave soldering process. In wave soldering process, the common failure encounter is insufficient solder barrel fill inside the PTH. This paper discusses and share the process characterizations defined for wave soldering with consideration of wave flux distribution and penetration, preheat rate and temperature, wave solder pot temperature, wave solder contact time and conveyor belt speed effects. The developed wave soldering process characterization have significant improved and overcome barrel fill insufficient solder challenge.

articleTitle: Challenges and Resolutions of 28nm Copper Wire Bond Process for Automotive Application
abstract: The 28nm low-K wafer with copper (Cu) wire bonding remains popular in IC packaging due to its cost-effectiveness and flexibility. This study aims to address the challenges in Cu wire bonding process development for 28nm wafer technology to meet the stringent requirements of the Automotive Electronics Council (AEC). The Dual Row Quad Flat No-lead (DRQFN) package was chosen as the test vehicle for its high I/O count, compact size, and superior thermal performance. The 28nm technology features a fine-pitch device with a 48.6μm bond pad opening (BPO), a 56μm bond pad pitch (BPP), and a 2.8μm thick aluminum (Al) bond pad. This study details solutions for achieving high intermetallic compound (IMC) coverage, consistent Al remnants under Cu ball bonds, and minimizing crevice formation through wire bonding optimization. A comprehensive Design of Experiments (DOE) was conducted to identify the optimal process window ensuring robustness in high-volume manufacturing. Additionally, a new inspection method using Backscattered SEM (BSSEM) on the Cu-Al IMC provided reliable reference data crucial for recipe optimization. The optimized wire bonding concept was validated through rigorous reliability assessments and proven to meet AEC requirements, as well as demonstrated a high assembly yield of over 99.5% in small volume monitoring.

articleTitle: Investigation of Laser Pulse Energy and Grinding Tool Characteristic on Marking Legibility of FOPLP
abstract: Recently, more players in the semiconductor industry have embarked on Fan Out Panel Level Packaging (FOPLP) due to key advantages in terms of lower packaging cost, higher performance and better components integration. As part of the manufacturing process of FOPLP, laser marking is done on Encapsulation Mold Compound (EMC) after grinding process. Therefore, marking legibility requires innovative characterization to achieve desired result. This study was conducted to investigate the marking legibility challenges in FOPLP and to find a creative solution that meets quality and cost expectation. Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) was used as a tool to recognize marking information and marking legibility beyond the coverage of JEDEC [1] requirement. According to this fundamental study, higher pulse energy with higher pulse frequency can have higher laser ablation rate for resin and filler (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), resulted in similar marking depth but good contrast and legibility. The mesh size of grinding wheel also played a role. A full matrix of Design of Experiment (DOE) was performed to fully characterize marking legibility performance and overcome limitation even on high warpage panel. Based on the comprehensive DOE results, laser marking energy density optimization, grinding wheel mesh size and laser marking with tape are the potential creative solutions to achieve good marking legibility on FOPLP.

articleTitle: Low- and Mid-Temperature Pb-Free Solder Preform Technology in Substrate Attach Application for Improved Thermomechanical Performance
abstract: New and emerging technologies such as e-mobility have a demand for higher power density, increased heat dissipation and higher reliability. The switch from Si die to SiC die to meet this requirement have placed importance on the selection of interconnect material within the power module package. In this paper, low to mid temperature Pb-free soldering solutions high-reliability alloys for high power density power electronics substrate attach to baseplate is discussed. Low temperature SAC-In alloys solution in solder preform configuration that can be used with reflow temperatures around 215-230 degree C in substrate attach soldering applications was presented to prevents re-melting of the interconnect soldering materials at die attach / clip attach during the step soldering process assembly. A mid temperature, high reliability Sn-based alloy solutions with reflow temperature around 260-270 degree C will also be presented as drop-in replacement for standard Pb- free SAC305 alloy for robust lifecycle performance comparable or better as shown by thermal shock testing data of -40°C to +125°C.

articleTitle: Strip Lasermarking Offset Marking Defect Improvement For Small Outline Packages
abstract: Strip-level laser marking is an assembly process to mark the units with product codes. This helps to eliminate mixed device issues. Offset marking is a defect of the laser marking process where the marked product code is shifted from the designated location on the units. This paper will address the issue of offset marking by doing improvement of the marking stage and clamper design to mitigate the lead frame warpage issue which causes the offset marking defect. Besides, this paper will also seek to eliminate the laser mark machine sequence in which, track motor homes when a different recipe is selected as the machine sequence indirectly contributes to the offset marking issue. After completion of the improvement actions, distance between the package edge to the marked alphabet on both sides of the units are measured by using microscope under 5x magnification. Then, the marking offset measurement is calculated by averaging the difference between both distances. Based on the data, it’s observed that mean and max measurement of offset marking have improved by 72 % 64% for the small outline packages. Conclusion, overall yield loss on offset marking is improved and defect was eliminated.

articleTitle: Warpage Simulation Including the Effect of Molding Compound Cure Shrinkage
abstract: Warpage control is the fundamental requirement for the packaging. The accurate prediction of warpage by finite element simulation becomes very critical during design stage. Intrinsic warpage is largely driven by coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch of packaging material. Cure shrinkage is one of the important features of the epoxy molding compound (EMC) and plays a very important role in warpage characterization. In previous simulation works, the cure shrinkage is combined with thermal shrinkage to obtain the total shrinkage of EMC, then derive the equivalent CTE from molding temperature to room temperature. One step warpage simulation is conducted by using this equivalent CTE to simulate the warpage at room temperature. But the warpage simulation accuracy is limited. In this paper, a multi-steps warpage simulation is proposed. Warpage caused by EMC cure shrinkage and by CTE1 and CTE2 are simulated separately. The final warpage is the combination of all warpages. The warpage of the EMC/Cu bi-layer beam specimens is measured and simulated by using both one-step and multi-steps methods. The simulation results are correlated with the warpage measured. Good agreement between measured warpage and multi-steps simulated warpage is obtained.

articleTitle: Enhancement of 8mm Carrier Tape Sealing Performance for Small Diode (SOD) Package via Carrier Tape Material and Sealing Shoe Selection
abstract: The packing of electronic components, particularly small outline diode (SOD) packages, is a crucial aspect of the manufacturing process that significantly impacts product quality and reliability. Enhancing the sealing performance of 8mm carrier tapes for SOD packages through the selection of appropriate carrier tape materials and sealing shoe configurations is vital for reducing conversion costs. However, the intricate design of the 8mm carrier tape relative to larger packages presents unique performance challenges. This study aims to optimize the sealing process by carefully selecting carrier tape materials, specifically Polystyrene (PS) and Polycarbonate (PC), and configuring the sealing shoe using a Design of Experiments (DOE) approach. Results demonstrate that increasing the size of the sealing shoe imprint enhances peel strength but reduces the clearance for unsealing. Our findings identify the optimal carrier tape material and sealing shoe design, offering significant implications for improving efficiency and reliability in the electronics sector.

articleTitle: Computational Fluid Dynamics Approach to Enhance Capillary Underfill Encapsulant Process in Heterogenous Package
abstract: Currently, flip-chip packaging technology, which connects semiconductor chips to substrates using solder bumps, is evolving alongside heterogeneous integration to achieve higher performance and efficiency. This paper examines the dynamics of capillary underfill flow in a configuration featuring three chips without solder bumps. The setup uses a substrate and consists of two chips of equal size and a third, larger chip, with chip thickness and spacing between the chips (Chip to Chip (1) and Chip to Chip (2)) at 22.29, 5.71, and 5.71, respectively. The research employs a thorough framework that considers the geometry, materials, and boundary conditions. The simulations model the behavior of incompressible and non-Newtonian fluids, enhancing computational efficiency by excluding the impact of temperature. Experimental validation confirms a strong correlation with the simulated underfill flow across various normalized time intervals. The study delves into the influence of underfill dispense weight and the length of the dispense, underscoring their relationship with the flow's progression and the time taken to reach the third chip. This investigation sheds light on how variations in these parameters affect the underfill flow in densely packed chip assemblies, thereby improving our understanding and informing the design of the underfill process for complex chip layouts.

articleTitle: FCLGA Study with Polymide (PI) Removal from Chip Surface
abstract: With the increasing demand for high-performance computing and the rapid development of advanced packaging, semiconductor product design has become even more crucial to meet high performance and reliability requirements. In pursuit of these goals, packaging assembly manufacturing requires substantial optimization in both process and material, especially in the presence of new IC design direction to adopt wafer surface without polyimide passivation as a form of simplification in wafer fabrication. A significant challenge is in optimizing the packaging assembly processes to improve adhesion between the epoxy mold compound material and the die interface, which decreases after the removal of die surface polyimide. Additionally, the removal of die surface polyimide can lead to interaction effects between the epoxy mold compound material and the die surface during molding process, potentially increasing the risk of ESD failure.This study focused on optimization of packaging assembly processes to overcome the adhesion challenges in IC chips without surface polyimide (PI). Flip Chip LGA was used a the test vehicle. The risk assessment analysis and corresponding process evaluation results were discussed in detail. Factors such as pre-mold plasma power, gas flow, time and mold transfer pressure were examined thoroughly to enhance the adhesion between the die top surface and the EMC (Epoxy Molding Compound) interface. The results revealed that, by optimizing the packaging assembly processes, the product could meet application and reliability requirements even with the die surface polyimide removal.In summary, optimization of manufacturing processes was proven to be effective in addressing the delamination risk caused by the removal of die surface polyimide, hence achieving the required product performance. This achievement enables simplification of wafer fabrication process which also supports sustainability effort.

articleTitle: Laser Ablation Dicing Revolutionizes Ultra-thin Wafer Saws Beyond the Capability of Blade Dicing
abstract: Driven by increasing power efficiency requirements in new advanced power electronic packages, the thickness of power semiconductor dies is decreasing. Fabricating ultra-thin wafers is the most direct and economic way to achieve improved power efficiency. Consequently, semiconductor companies are exploring silicon wafer thicknesses below 50 μm, which may have already reached the capability of blade dicing. Issues such as metal peeling at the side walls of dies and large bottom side die chipping sizes are always the bottlenecks for ultra-thinned wafers when using the common blade dicing technology. This study presents a comprehensive investigation on laser ablation dicing technology to overcome these issues. The process characterizations of laser ablation dicing on 50 μm thick wafers along with validation on 30 μm thick wafers are discussed. Additionally, solutions to reduce die strength concerns caused by laser ablation dicing are presented, too. Results indicate that laser ablation dicing is effective in the range of 30 μm to 75 μm wafer thickness and down to-30 μm narrowed saw street width, where the capability intersection between laser ablation and blade dicing is at the thickness of 50 μm and the saw street’s width of 60 μm.

articleTitle: Refined Wire Bond Pad Cratering Testing Method
abstract: Wire bonding is crucial in semiconductor packaging to create electrical connections from the die to the package using fine wires typically made up of copper or gold. However, unoptimized first bond parameters, specifically mechanical force and ultrasonic energy, can cause cracks in the interlayer dielectric (ILD) within the die, leading to electrical discontinuities and device reliability issues. Thus, Joint Test Action Group (JTAG) communication and leakage failures during electrical testing often signify ILD cracks which are further verified by destructive pad cratering test through chemical etching. Generally, good units yield clear bond pads, while those with ILD cracks exhibit dimples due to unevenness from metal layer separation. However, recent leaded quad flat package lots presented inconclusive pad cratering results due to abnormal brownish bond pads, attributed to their unique die structure where the barrier metal rests on a softer metal layer, M7, instead of the typical ILD which is harder. Due to reduced support, the barrier metal is more prone to minor cracks or pinholes, allowing the etching chemical to penetrate, dissolve the M7 layer underneath, and expose subsequent layers. This vulnerability led to the refinement of the current pad cratering testing method through modifications of testing parameters such as the etching solution, soaking temperature and duration, and incorporating ultrasonic cleaning along with its solution. Results obtained demonstrated the effectiveness in detecting the presence of ILD cracks and were further verified through cross-section analysis and attribute measurement system analysis (MSA). This refinement resulted in a remarkable 74% reduction in scrap cost compared to the baseline method.

articleTitle: Decoupling Capacitor Booster Module
abstract: Intel CPU (Central Processing Unit) compute performance is influenced by the Load Line (LL) number, which is determined by the number of capacitors placed on the motherboard (MB). Adding more capacitors to achieve a better LL for higher core performance requires extra board area, potentially compromising battery size and impacting battery life. Additionally, maintaining platform compatibility for reuse over multiple generations can be challenging. Compatibility is disrupted when additional capacitors are needed for performance improvements in future products, necessitating a motherboard redesign, which affects the schedule and incurs additional costs. Redesigning a MB can vary significantly based on complexity and resources, which may take up to at least one quarter of a year. Accelerated development will also need a minimum of 8 weeks. The cost of the client motherboard also varies significantly based on the model and features, which can range from a few hundred dollars to more than a thousand dollars. The idea here is to have a Decoupling Capacitor Booster Module (DCBM) which is used to attach to the main MB to boost power delivery with those extra capacitors on the module. The capacitors on the DCBM need to be placed directly aligned vertically with the corresponding capacitors on the MB to get the best effectiveness by having the shortest loop inductance path to the package BGA. The DCBM takes advantage of the available Z-height and can be placed on the top or bottom side of the MB, or on both sides. Positioning capacitors on top of the DCBM is expected to be as effective as placing them on the main MB.

articleTitle: Influence of moisture variation on SAC405 solder ball oxidation characteristic in WLCSP
abstract: Solder bump oxidation has been one of the concerns of poor wettability during FC bonding or SMT process. It is known that high temperature and/or high humidity environment will continuously accelerate solder bump oxidation over long storage/staging time. The result of solder bump oxidation is discoloration which can be observed via naked eye or by optical microscope. In order to understand the severity of bump discoloration, various level of discolored bump samples were sent for surface analysis to measure the solder oxidation thickness. These samples were subjected to XPS for oxide depth profiling. This analysis is trying to create a bump oxidation severity table based on the degree of bump discoloration. By referring to bump oxidation severity table, a study was conducted to analyze the main factors that contribute to discolored bump. In this study, factors such as numbers of wafer in FOSB, moisture-barrier bag (MBB) packing method and wafer drying time were investigated. Due to the fact that bump oxidation was never found at bumping line before MBB packing, bump oxidation is suspected to occur during transportation and/or during storage at warehouse. Our experiment result indicates that the moisture trapped inside wafer re-passivation material can be easily released and condensed inside the FOSB container under low temperature condition. The condensed moisture inside FOSB will accelerate bump oxidation process even after the environment is returned to room temperature.

articleTitle: Alpha Emission Rate Characterization and Risk Evaluation of Substrate Materials Used in Memory Packages
abstract: As the memory components are developed with continuously package downsizing, their soft error rates become more susceptible to the alpha particles induced from packaging materials. For the purpose to meet reliable performance of advanced memory products, packaging material suppliers are demanded to develop the materials to lower alpha emission rate (AER). The AER of the materials such as underfill, solder bump and pre-solder had been investigated in flip chip components with active side downward. However, the AER of the substrate materials like solder resist and core are rarely discussed and could be potentially resources of alpha particles, which may increase the soft error rate as the bump height and die gap are shrunk. In this paper, the AER of substrate materials are measured with different layered structures by using alpha particle counting system. Two types of cores (ultra-low and normal CTE ranges) performed different AER, which may be induced by different impurities in compositions. The effects of Cu foil coverage rate and thickness on substrate AER are also studied. Furthermore, the Monte Carlo simulation code is applied to calculate the emissive paths from substrate materials by considering energies detected from AER spectrum, isotopes decay series, and to further determine the risk of alpha particles in flip chip package.

articleTitle: Intel’s Affordable Industrial Internet of Things(IoT) for Equipment Predictive Maintenance
abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving industrial landscape, predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as critical strategy to minimize downtime, reduce cost and avoid quality excursion. Intel has been using a standardized Industrial Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure in Intel’s Assembly test and fabrication facilities (ATM & Fab) for several years. Most of the legacy factory equipment wasn’t built with the digital sensors, so it is does not generate useful equipment data log to monitor tool health condition. This abstract present a comprehensive overview of how the internet of things (IoT)is revolutionizing the predictive maintenance practices across Intel factories.This paper describes Intel IoT infrastructure and the central IoT dashboard including data acquisition, data transmission, Cloud MQTT broker, and data analytics. It also discusses the integration of advance analytics such as machine learning and big data analytics, can be a powerful tool to help us better diagnose and perform predictive maintenance. These insights empower organizations to make informed decisions, optimize maintenance schedules and allocate resources more efficiently.Our standardized Industrial Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructure is highly scalable and has numerous business benefits:•Zero excursions- Scrap avoidance•Real time conditional health monitoring•Cost savings- spare part lifespan•min unscheduled downtime

articleTitle: Effect of Fluorine Implant Energy on the Performance of P+/N-Junction, Poly-Si Resistor, and PMOS
abstract: This study investigates the enhancement of Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (CMOS) technology electrical characteristics and reliability through the co-implantation of Fluorine with Boron Fluoride (BF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The effects of Fluorine implantation on three devices - P+/N-junction, P+ Poly-resistors, and PMOS transistors are explored. The results show that higher Fluorine implant energies increase leakage currents at P+/N-junctions while having a comparable breakdown voltage. In contrast, the P+ Poly sheet resistance decreases with increasing Fluorine implant energy at different measurement temperatures, with a minimum Temperature Coefficient of Resistance (TCR) achievable at specific Fluorine implant energies. Furthermore, in PMOS devices, higher Fluorine implant energies improve Drain-Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL) around 20% and reduce approximately 3% of Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) degradation. The electrical characteristics of PMOS, such as threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) increase, Flat band voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FB</inf>) and transconductance (g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>) decrease due to the Oxide thickness (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ox</inf>) increase by implanting high Fluorine energy. This study reveals that high Fluorine energy with BF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is a viable co-implantation for optimizing CMOS process integration scheme.

articleTitle: Manufacturability of A Novel Vertical Interconnect Design for High-Speed Signaling
abstract: A novel and patent-pending vertical interconnect that allows design customization from manufacturing perspective while meeting the impedance target of high-speed input/output interfaces (HSIOs) is the core of this paper. Plated- Through-Holes (PTHs) of Type-3 printed circuit board (PCB) are generally designed with physical dimensions that are dictated by manufacturing process. They are not designed with electrical performance as a consideration factor. As such, PTH impedance which can be as low as 70Ω for HSIO buses would have huge mismatch with transmission lines which are designed with ideal 85Ω for example. This translates to significant signaling performance impact. The vertical interconnect structure described in this paper is therefore innovated to meet the electrical requirement. This research is an extension of previously published technical papers that address and neutralize the electrical impairments caused by PTHs in Type-3 PCB. Specifically, this paper is focused on demonstrating the correlation between simulation and measurement results via test coupons of the said innovation, as well as definition of design rules that uses existing standard manufacturing process without incurring significant cost-adder.

articleTitle: Moisture Effect on Adhesion Between Polybenzoxazole and Sputtering Titanium in WLCSP
abstract: The mechanism of moisture effect on the bumping process in Wafer Level Chip Scale Package (WLCSP) was investigated, to understand the influence of moisture on the interfacial adhesion between Polybenzoxazole (PBO) and Sputtering Titanium. Residue Gas Analyzer (RGA) tool was used for PBO outgassing measurement during de-gassing step, Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP) step and Titanium (Ti) sputtering step. Focused Ion Beam (FIB) and Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) were used to study interfacial adhesion performance. According to statistical analysis of the investigation result, it was found that PBO-Ti interfacial adhesion is correlated to the idling time of PBO plasma clean to oven baking. The longer the idling time, the more moisture will be absorbed, that will directly impact the adhesion of PBO and sputtering Ti. The investigation shows good adhesion when idling time is well controlled. Furthermore, it is also correlated to de-gas temperature of sputtering process. The higher the degas temperature, the more water (H2O) volatilization amount will be detected by RGA, which indicated less moisture remained in the PBO. Less moisture absorption will reduce delamination detected by FIB and SEM. Therefore, the optimized de-gas temperature and idling time must be well controlled in WLCSP bumping process flow. This investigation provided a breakthrough guideline of process control in order to achieve good PBO-Ti interfacial adhesion.

articleTitle: Effective Approach to Achieve Zero Interfacial Delamination on High-Power Automotive Devices After Reliability Test
abstract: The demands of high-power devices for automotive applications are rising rapidly, especially with the booming sales of electric vehicles in recent years. Nevertheless, the interfacial delamination of devices under stringent reliability stresses is often an issue to the manufacturers. To address this issue, lead frame roughening technology is usually employed to improve the interfacial adhesions through mechanical interlocking mechanisms. While this method is generally applicable, it incurs sizeable equipment footprints during mass production with processes including pre-cleaning, roughening, and post-cleaning of the lead frames. Additionally, the usage of hazardous chemicals in the lead frame roughening technology may pose environmental and safety concerns. In this study, a simple yet economical adhesion promoter coating approach is proposed to improve the interfacial adhesion for high-power silicon carbide (SiC) automotive devices. Unlike the roughening technology which only focuses on lead frame surfaces, the adhesion promoter is coated on all molding surfaces including lead frame, wire, solder and die surfaces. This total molding surface coating inclusiveness is essential to eliminate the seed of delamination to grow from all possible interfaces. As a result, the coated automotive devices can achieve zero delamination after the stringent IPC/JEDEC moisture sensitivity level (MSL) 1 conditioning.

articleTitle: Development of Robust Cu Wire Looping for Small Sensor QFN Package with Higher Dual Die Stack
abstract: Complex requirement for automotive accelerometer sensors new product development requires continuous innovation in QFN Cu wire bonding process. In this paper, an innovative thorough method to develop wire loop height and loop shape was developed to meet small QFN with package size 3x3mm with >40% dual die stack height increase vs. conventional product. Long wire length in terms of x, y, z direction has been studied on various loop type including forward and reverse bonding. The result of this study showed an optimized wire loop recipe can be achieved with zero wire short versus less optimized version which can cause as high as 36% wire short. The optimized wire loop recipe has been established and validated by T0 post mold test thus enabling a robust assembly process for small QFN sensor packages with significantly higher stacked die height.

articleTitle: Functional Validation on Complex Power Integrity Network Design
abstract: With the recent introduction of disaggregated die architecture, power delivery network (PDN) performance expectations have shifted, from previously self-induced noise to concurrent workload noise. In pre-silicon simulation environment, it is rather challenging to accurately predict such workload conditions. In this paper, a new testing methodology is added to test disaggregated PDN architecture. Knowing that multiple High-Speed Input Output (HSIO) ports like PCIe4 and USB4 when stressed with concurrent traffic will have an impact on receiver (Rx) jitter. Instead of the traditional electrical validation approach, the team used a functional validation test bench, and validated using real world traffic scenarios; to stimulate power management of multiple different HSIOs concurrency for several weeks, while also resulting in a surprisingly small receiver margin degradation. The paper will conclude PDN improvement and validation coverage recommendations for future disaggregated architecture, knowing this is becoming the new computing trend.

articleTitle: Deposition of AlGaN thin film using HIPIMS and RF co-sputtering technique
abstract: HIPIMS which is known by high-power impulse magnetron sputtering is an advanced thin film fabrication technique used in materials science and semiconductor industries. In HIPIMS, a high voltage pulse is applied to a sputter target, creating a high-density plasma composed of metal ions and electrons. This intense plasma bombardment results in highly efficient sputtering of the target material, allowing for precise and uniform deposition of thin films onto substrates. In this study, aluminium gallium nitride thin films were fabricated using low N2/(Ar+ N2)% ratio of gas flow. Then through the analysis using field-emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and atomic force microscopy (AFM), the surface morphologies of aluminium gallium nitride (AlGaN) film were studied at various nitrogen (N2) flow rates. XRD results show that AlGaN films deposited exhibit polycrystalline and Al structure depending on the composition of N2 flow. The the AlGaN films surface roughness were smooth and had lower roughness at N2 flow rates concentration of 10 to 50%. At 50% of N2 flow rates, the surface morphology of AlGaN films deposited was uniform and the grain size was small. Results indicated that low ratio of N2 flow by using the HIPIMS technique provides a significant effect on AlGaN thin films deposition.

articleTitle: Industrialization of a New Adhesion Promoter Process for Leadframe
abstract: Substrate-based microelectronics have become common these days, but leadframe-based packages are still widely used in the semiconductor industry. Increased reliability requirements have led to extensive adoptions of "adhesion promoter" technologies on leadframes, to enhance the adhesion between leadframe metal surfaces and chip encapsulation materials, such as epoxy molding compounds (EMC). With the introduction of the most stringent requirement of the automotive electronics industry, many plastic packages, such as QFP, tend to show their weaknesses in delamination even during early reliability.Some degree of EMC delamination is usually found near the lead bonding areas on the leadframe, which are typically Ag-plated and Ag surfaces have very poor adhesion to EMC. If gold wires were used as the interconnects between the die and the leadframe, the gold wires may still be intact after package preconditioning due to their high ductility properties. Driven by cost initiatives, Cu wires have been introduced to replace gold wires. Cu wire introduction brings several workability challenges that require specific process optimizations on each leadframe finish [1]. Under such circumstances, severe problems of stitch bond cracks could occur and lead to serious package reliability issues due to the lower elongation of Cu wires.EMC adhesion can be improved acting on leadframe finishing: different plating stacks or roughening techniques can achieve a better adhesion, however those solutions will imply a significant leadframe cost increase, as well as the workability during IC assembly processes. In this paper, we will share the major challenges faced during the industrialization of a new adhesion promoter process, which is applicable to Ag surfaces and do not require surface etching or roughening; this study will also address the ultimate adhesion performance at high temperature of the new adhesion promoter and other key benefits of this noble process.

articleTitle: Study of Glue Creeping Behavior On Die Surface for Thin Die Using Roughen Pre-plated Leadframe
abstract: Many Dual Row Quad Flat No Lead (DRQFN) Radio Frequency (RF) semiconductor packages today require thin die to achieve better RF performance. This has posed a challenge for die attach glue creeping onto die surface which can cause wirebond-ability issue. The situation is even more challenging when Anti-Epoxy Bleed Out (Anti-EBO) is being applied on roughen pre-plated (RT-PPF) lead frame, where the epoxy bleed out to the lead frame side is being mitigated but has worsened the glue creeping onto die surface. Although this problem can be minimized by selecting non-roughen lead frame surface, but it will create high risk for package delamination, causing the product to be unable to meet the stringent package reliability requirement. In this paper, a comprehensive study was conducted including glue material behavior prior to oven curing, the staging time window control between die attach and oven cure process, and snap cure prior to oven cure. The result of the study showed that snap cure is able to partially cure the glue and freeze the resin bleed-out, which allowed longer staging time for more production flexibility, hence enabling higher manufacturability and process robustness for DRQFN with thin die on Anti-EBO lead frame.

articleTitle: Signal and Power integrity challenges in PCB for System-on-chip(SoC) based automotive applications and the need for chiplet based designs
abstract: In this paper, the challenges of signal and power integrity in PCB for integration of SoC based automotive applications IC’s are evaluated using market based EDA tools. Several key parameters like crosstalk, channel loss, timing, voltage drop, current density, Power distribution network and plane resonances are studied to investigate their impacts on the SI, PI and EMC performance in the PCB. The growing trend of the automotive industry needs customization, modularity, and scalability of IC for its performance. This paper also addresses the need for Chiplet based designs in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Impacts of Saw Blade Selection, Dressing and Dicing Parameters on Die Sidewall Quality
abstract: Dicing is a critical process step in semiconductor packaging flow to separate wafer into individual chip. Despite the insurgence of new dicing technologies like plasma dicing, stealth dicing and laser full cut, traditional mechanical saw remains the most widely used method because of its low cost of ownership as it is widely used by assembly sites, process maturity, wide selection of equipment and blade offerings. For Wafer Level Chip Scale Packaging (WLCSP), as dicing quality is extremely critical to ensure there is no chipping and crack propagation after unit is being mounted onto customer board, die sidewall quality is usually being inspected during tape and reel process. Besides chipping, cosmetic defect like heavy saw mark will cause overkill and unwanted yield loss. In this paper, we investigated various factors that are affecting die sidewall quality from blade selection, dressing and sawing parameters to reduce chipping and overkill reject. Detailed Failure Analysis (FA) was performed on the defective unit and saw blade. Coupled with detailed analysis on spindle vibration data, these have helped us to nail down the die crack mechanism that correlates to saw blade profile and dressing parameters used. Subsequently, a series of Design of Experiment (DOE) was performed to reduce saw mark overkill rate during tape and reel process sidewall inspection.

articleTitle: Exploration on Miniaturization of Immersion Cooling Technology for Client Desktop and Edge Devices
abstract: Small Form Factor (SFF) systems often face thermal limitations due to the constraints of the chassis space. This paper aims to bring liquid immersion cooling technology into client/edge desktop segments, with the intent of miniaturization without trading off the performance. A self-contained liquid immersion cooling approach has been developed for desktop/IOT systems. The system chassis is designed with compartmentalization as a standalone form factor system. The heat source distribution, liquid flow, and the liquid cooling heat sink have been optimized. The prototyped solution has demonstrated a cooling capability of 650W, showing a path for Intel® Xeon® Scalable Processors family CPUs to get into a Small Form Factor (SFF) PC.

articleTitle: Analytical Approach for Preliminary Deformation Investigation
abstract: The objective of this study is to compare the results from experiment and modeling on simplified models with those from analytical solution. The target is to understand if simple analytical models or tools can be used for fast indication and preliminary evaluation of material behavior. Simple samples and respective models will be built and evaluated for warpage at temperatures of interest, namely room temperature and reflow temperature. Following this an analytical approach using Timoshenko beam formula will be evaluated and results compared with the experimental and modeling results. Finally, it will be decided if and how a simplified tool can be developed for fast and preliminary results for material comparison basis as a means of eliminating material that will not reach the desired performance prior to building more elaborate models or samples. The analysis focuses on bi-material structures for the time being and hence is more suited as a rough estimate for frame based packages, though an example for a Ball Grid Array (BGA) package is also presented. The assumptions and limitations of this methodology will be outlined. Keywords—packaging, thermo-mechanical modeling, Timoshenko equation, warpage, finite element analysis (FEA), package design, analytics (key words)

articleTitle: Galvanic corrosion behavior of Ag-filled electrically conductive adhesive on Sn-plated of surface mount chip resistor
abstract: The present paper investigated the corrosion behavior of electrically conductive adhesives (ECAs) on tin (Sn)-plated surface mount chip resistors with epoxy mold compound (EMC)in integrated circuit (IC) packaging. Test samples were assembled by a chip resistor with Tin plating outer terminal attached by Ag-filled electrically conductive adhesive then encapsulated by EMC. Three stimulants temperature, moisture and electrical bias were applied during reliability testing (Moisture Sensitivity Level, Temperature Humidity Bias, Unbiased Highly Accelerated Stress Test ) to accelerate galvanic corrosion. As long as no delamination after MSL was observed, no tin corrosion/oxidation was observed after THB and UHST. The resistance value after UHST 400hrs was comparable with unstressed samples. The overall results show that galvanic corrosion could be avoided by assembling the product without any internal delamination. Currently, IC packaging uses optimized process parameters and state of the art materials which increase product robustness (no delamination) avoiding the formatting of local electrolytes that enables the migration of ions from higher to lower electron potential, causing corrosion

articleTitle: Chemical Identification of sub 10-µm defects and contamination in packaging
abstract: Contamination and defects in microelectronic packages can have deleterious effects to device reliability and usability. With increasingly smaller feature sizes, pitch and sophisticated advanced packaging and components, such as interposers, FOWLP and FOPLP, even miniscule defects and contaminations are increasingly effective in disabling devices. With feature sizes of dark-colored contamination and defects in the order of submicron to 10 micrometers, conventional Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) and Raman microscopes would not provide sufficient spatial resolution and sensitivity for meaningful root-cause analyses in the past few decades. In recent years, a new pump-probe excitation-detection chemical analysis concept offering sub-micron spatial resolution in Optical PhotoThermal InfraRed microscopic instrumentation (O-PTIR) has been developed to address the needs for high spatial resolution and ultra-high sensitivity analyses in a non- contact reflection-based operation manner. To further speed up analysis of chemically complex specimen, co-located auto- fluorescence imaging of specimen can be further exploited to qualitatively assess its spatio-chemical distribution before conducting sub-micron infrared analysis on the same sample stage of the instrument. Best of all, auto-fluorescence poses no ill-effects to the quality of O-PTIR spectra. In this contribution, we will detail the enabling concept and relevant case studies, covering examples including underfill cross-sections and contamination on metal pads.

articleTitle: Base loop characterization to alleviate short tail issue in stack die package
abstract: NAND flash drive is a form of non-volatile memory storage technology that does not require power to store large memory capacity. With solid-state drives (SSDs), multiple NAND dies can be stacked together. The higher the number of dies, the higher the capacity of memory stored. Multi-stack NAND dies require die-to-die bonding using Au wire to form a closed electrical circuit. Die-to-die bonding, also called cascade bonding, forms cascade wires by landing the second bond to the top surface of the ball bond from the bottom die stack. This unstable surface imposes a challenge to bond the second bond due to its unevenness. In multi-stack devices, short tail in Au wire bonding challenges the bonders' efficiency and productivity. Short tail occurs when wire prematurely tears before reaching the desired tail length after second bond formation, resulting in too short or no tail for the next FAB formation. Hence, this paper analyses the factors and mechanism of short tails and highlights the innovative solution to develop a more robust looping formation for cascade wire bonding. Parameters namely the first and second kink, loop base and desirable second bond offset were optimized to eliminate short tails, creating a more stable process.

articleTitle: PFAS free die attach for robust manufacturability of large body semiconductor packages
abstract: The recent regulation around PFAS has prompted many suppliers to rethink their offerings in terms of greener and sustainable solutions. In die attach, Quad Flat No lead (QFN) packages in large body format represent one of the steadiest growing types of chip carriers. Owing to their low profile, condensed form factor, high I/O and high thermal dissipation they are popular choices for chip set consolidation, miniaturization, and chips with high power density. There is demand for continued improvements in reliability of QFNs. Compatibility with flexible manufacturing and broad latitude performances are key areas that are critical for large body QFN type devices in Auto and RF markets.

articleTitle: Automotive High Power Flip Chip Quad Flat No-leads Package Robustness Study
abstract: FCQFN (Flip Chip Quad Flat No-leads) package is common for automotive high power products in electronics industry especially for thermal efficiency. Although the packaging process is not complicated and it has thinner body size than the traditional wire bond QFN package, there are some challenges in the packaging development. Among the challenges that can affect the final performance of the package, delamination is a common one. Therefore, in this study, the investigation of the delamination behavior in automotive high power FCQFNs is conducted to identify the delamination mechanism. The package size of FCQFN in this study is 5*5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The chip is connected to the Ag-plated pad of the metal lead by Cu pillar bump and encapsulated by mold compound to provide physical protection. The package performance was validated by MSL3 (Moisture Sensitivity Level 3) and thermal cycling upto 2000 cycles. During early development stage, Through-scan results showed obvious delamination which concentrated at die paddle areas with shorter half etching and without tie bar. Moreover, the cross-sectional results showed the delamination occurred between die paddle sidewall and mold compound. In addition, thermal mechanical modeling indicated the high stress area at delamination position. The stress reduction was predicted by modeling and verified by empirical result. Based on the experimental results, delamination can be significantly improved by increasing die paddle half etching width which is a simple and breakthrough solution. Finally, the delamination mechanism is concluded to be insufficient contact area between short etched die paddle and mold compound. The die paddle with longer half etching width design has shown to be greatly effective in mitigating the risk of delamination, hence ensuring a robust automotive high power FCQFN package.

articleTitle: Innovative RF Shield Rework Method for Wireless Module in Ultrathin Notebook
abstract: A breakthrough cost effective rework method for RF(Radio Frequency) shield with lower cycle time has been developed which is using hot plate rework equipment together with a customized hot plate fixture to remove and place the RF shield onto the PCB. The basic principle that has been applied on the new rework method for RF shield is conduction heat transfer whereby the heat transfer rate is higher if compared to the convection heat transfer that being used in conventional reflow process with rework machine. The rework cycle time will be reduced with higher heat transfer rate during rework to melt the RF shield solder joint. The cycle time of the rework process with the hot plate fixture to melt the RF shield solder joint has been successfully reduced significantly by ~82%. In term of rework cost reduction, based on the cost saving calculation for one of the wireless module products after using this innovative RF shield rework method, the rework cost has been reduced by ~80%. This paper will review the design of the customized hot plate fixture, the conduction heat transfer concept with the hot plate rework machine and detail of the removal and placement of the RF shield.

articleTitle: Pressure and Pressure-less Cu Sintering Paste Developed for Next Generation Interconnection Material
abstract: Because of their high thermal and electrical conductivity, copper (Cu) sintering pastes were developed to meet the requirements for high-power applications. Compared to mature silver (Ag) sintering pastes, which are also designed for high-power applications, the Cu sintering paste advantages, such as low cost and insusceptibility to Ag migration, are appealing. Through extensive research, another important feature for Cu sintering paste was found: Cu sintering paste sinters well on bare Cu. In other words, no special precious metal plating (e.g. gold (Au) or Ag) is required for die or activate metal brazing (AMB). This eliminates the step of plating with Au or Ag for die or AMB and can potentially reduce costs. In this paper, pressure and pressure-less Cu sinter pastes with high-reliability were developed for high-power applications. The bonding performance of both pastes was determined on the Cu substrate. At 250-270°C, 15-25 MPa, 3-7.5 min, and under a nitrogen (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2)</inf> atmosphere, the pressure Cu sintering paste reached 40-70 MPa shear strength. For pressureless Cu sintering paste, a shear strength of >25 MPa was demonstrated under the sintering conditions of 250°C, 30 min, and an N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> atmosphere. Meanwhile, both pressure and pressureless Cu pastes have passed 1,000 cycles of thermo-cycling tests (TCT) (-65-150°C), which indicates its high-reliability.

articleTitle: Introduction To Power Tunnel Innovation In PCB & Package For Better Platform Power Delivery
abstract: Intel's "Project EVO" represents a leap forward in compact PC design, focusing on maximizing space efficiency and performance within laptops. Central to this initiative is the reduction of component sizes, with a special emphasis on streamlining the power delivery system. By minimizing the footprint of power planes on Printed Circuit Boards (PCB), it makes room for critical elements such as cooling fans and battery packs. Our key innovation is the power tunnel concept, which transforms PCB and package design. This approach consolidates power planes from adjacent layers into a singular power tunnel, increasing the current carrying capacity and improves load line while simultaneously allowing for a more compact form factor. This breakthrough aids in improving power integrity and cost reduction (by decreasing the number of package layers and PCB board size). Both the board and package prototypes have successfully integrated the power tunnel innovation without incurring fabrication risks. The board design's power performance has been confirmed, and data collection for the package design is underway, with results expected by the second half of 2024. The power tunnel method is set to be a transformative development in the realm of compact PC design, marking a significant stride towards more powerful PC.

articleTitle: Investigation of Package Delamination Behavior in Large Quad Flat No-Lead Package
abstract: Package delamination is a common challenge in large Quad Flat No-Lead (QFN) packages. This study investigates delamination behavior in QFNs with Ag-plated leadframes to identify the delamination mechanism. The QFN package size in this study is 11x11 mm, with the chip's Al pad connected to the Ag-plated pins of the metal leadframe by copper wire. In the final step, the chip on the metal carrier with copper wire is encapsulated by a generic mold compound (EMC) for physical protection. Scanning Acoustic Tomography (SAT) was used to identify the location and degree of delamination. Preliminary SAT results during initial development revealed significant delamination concentrated at the Ag-plated stitch finger area. Cross-sectional inspection results indicated the fracture position occurred between the mold compound and Ag layers. As the adhesion between pure Ag and the mold compound can be improved by increasing the Ag oxide thickness, this study showed that increasing die bond curing temperature by 30°C and wire bond temperature by 20°C increased Ag oxide thickness from 1.75 nm to 2.15 nm. Moisture Sensitivity Level 3 (MSL3) results revealed significant improvement in delamination. Additionally, the experiment indicated the impact of plasma cleaning on delamination. Finally, reducing the Ag plating area on the leadframe by 20% exposed roughened copper, effectively enhancing the mold compound's adhesion to the leadframe, providing a complete solution against delamination.

articleTitle: New Enhanced Loop Formation for Compute DRAM Package: An Innovative Solution to Enhance Robustness of Wire Loop and Enable Design Rule Limitation
abstract: The extend of this paper covers Compute DRAM (Dynamic Random Access Memory) package with the single DRAM die attached in a BOC (board on chip) package. In this package the lead is located above the die, thus a relatively high loop will be required. This condition is set to avoid the wire-to-lead short due to the insufficient gap. In addition, die placement become a concern by which offset of the die placement increases the risk of wire touching the adjacent lead, which violate the wire bond design rule. Standard loop is unable to support a high loop as it will result in wire sweep. Hence, the PSL (Power Series Low) loop is an innovative approach to enable the design rule limitation by increasing the wire loop height in a stable condition which no sign of stress at ball neck and zero wire short reject.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study on Real Time Electrostatic Charge Monitoring in Wafer Form Process with Potential Triboelectrification Motion at Dicing Saw
abstract: In dicing saw process, electrostatic charge is generated mostly at the spinner section due to frictional electrification owing to cleaning with deionized water, drying with dry air and separation electrification during workpiece separated from spinner table. The change phenomena of electrostatic charges held on workpiece throughout the triboelectrification motion is crucial yet without any inline monitor triggering system. Thus dicing saw machine spinner section was selected as primary feasibility study for real time electrostatic charge monitoring with the help of fault detection and classification (FDC). By communicating the electrostatic sensors with host system and FDC, several FDC window modelling able to setup for live data monitoring. Electrostatic charge trend study was conducted with different ionizer air flowrates and deionized water resistivity to validate the effectiveness of the inline monitoring system. With appropriate FDC triggering limit, this inline monitoring system is capable to detect any degraded or faulty ionizer, abnormal workpiece electrostatic charge, wrong ionizer settings and abnormal water resistivity while providing signal and data trend for electrostatic charges behavior. With this shift left approach and mechanism, electrostatic discharge (ESD) event can be detected early to minimize and reduce the losses and cost of scrap.

articleTitle: Wafer Level Plasma as An Alternative for Wafer Pre Thin Process
abstract: As the memory industry continue to evolve and grow with market size valued at USD 104.58 billion in 2022 and the worldwide semiconductor memory market is expected to reach USD 201.91 billion by 2032, simultaneously the industry continues to grow with the complexity of new wafer tech nodes with requirements of thinner die based on the demanding application needs of higher storage and processing capacity of single chip. This fuels the requirement to venture into SDBG (Stealth Dicing Before Grinding) process as it provides solution of increased in the number of dies per wafer due smaller saw street requirements and improved die strength which plays an important role for thin die application. The wafer Pre-Thinning process log point is unique to Micron application of the SDBG, this is a requirement as currently backend assembly wafers are received with backside film which is not removed during the wafer fabrication process at front end. The removal of the film is vital for the SDBG as it impacts the laser penetration during the stealth dicing process. This paper fully explores wafer level plasma (Fig 1) as an alternative method in the backside film removal rather than using mechanical grinding to remove the backside film. This paper also collects the feasibility data of such applications.

articleTitle: Die Placement Process Optimization in Reducing Occurrence of Solder Short between Flip-Chip Die Pad
abstract: This study investigates the occurrence of solder shorts in a new System-in-Package (SiP) product during the setup phase in Inari, specifically related to a flip-chip die with a tighter solder bump pad pitch. Despite no abnormalities in the employed processes, an increasing number of solder shorts were observed. The study details a series of process optimizations conducted to restore the yield to an acceptable level. Within the SMT processes, certain process parameters, including those related to solder printing, flip-chip die placement, and solder paste reflow, were identified as potentially contributing to the solder short occurrences. Various evaluations and optimizations were performed, ruling out most variants and pinpointing the impact speed parameter setting during die placement as a significant factor influencing solder short incidence between flip-chip die pads.

articleTitle: Cost Effective Hostless System for Add-In-Card (AIC) Post-Silicon Electrical Validation
abstract: Graphic Processing Unit (GPU) post silicon validation is executed on reference board in PCIe Add-In Card form factor via PCIe x16 edge gold finger. The GPU reference board is designed to assemble on a Client or Server board via PCIEx16 interface which will be similar to actual product form factor. Hence in the current validation environment, the test setup is usually space consuming and incurs higher station setup cost as it requires a Client or Server board pairing to power up the small GPU card. The innovation here is a hostless concept for GPU card coupled with a custom-design PCIe adaptor board with x16 connector and necessary voltage and clock requirements of the PCIe edge finger. ATX Power Supply connects to adaptor board and 100MHz clock supply from Clock integrated chip as RefCLK. With voltage supply and clock, GPU intellectual property (IP) block can power up via running bootscript through eXtended Debug Port (XDP) on JTAG to access GPU and its IP block registry. GPU reference board connects to PCIe x16 connector on adaptor board. ATX Power supply connects to PCIe adaptor board and turns power on. Setup connection is simple and eliminates host board, provides flexibility in standalone setup, cost effective and power on the GPU for specific GPU IP validation and GPU debug, except PCIe IP validation which need PCIe host communication. This replaces 60% of host system in conventional test setup per program, resulting in savings of USD2K per setup, USD20K per program. Setup connection is simple, saves workbench space by 50%.

articleTitle: Real time inferencing of semiconductor wafer probing process using Machine Learning
abstract: The Wafer Sort process in Semiconductor Manufacturing identifies die defects before assembly into packages. A wafer prober verifies each die on a wafer by making precise electrical-mechanical connections between thousands of die bumps with probe tips finer than a human hair. Poor contact could damage these bumps or even break underlying circuitry causing yield losses or reliability defects. Previous state-of-the-art utilized statistical process control systems based on historical electrical failure baselines to identify degraded probers. Flagged probers require costly repair procedures that consume man-hours and metrology tools to verify probe length, planarity, and conductivity.Accuracy of the past method reduced significantly for smaller device dimensions of advanced process nodes that are increasingly susceptible to fab variations. A stable historical baseline took long to establish and often could not be conclusively determined, resulting in thousands of repair hours and millions in capital costs spent annually debugging invalid alarms. Our work rearchitected the past method with a machine learning based defect detection solution. By comprehending wafer spatial locations of different electrical failures, we achieved real time inferencing of upstream fab defects versus genuine prober issues requiring repairs. This novel approach demonstrated consistently high defect classification accuracy in high volume manufacturing.

articleTitle: The Challenges and Solutions to the Development of Light Shielding Mask Glass from Design Phase to Process Optimization for CMOS Image Sensors
abstract: This paper discusses the introduction of light shielding masks (LSM) in image sensor applications for glare reduction purpose, focusing on the challenges in the dicing process due to the uneven LSM surface. This paper focuses on a rectangular anti-reflective borosilicate glass and evaluates two LSM glass mounting methods: faced-up and faced-down. The faced-up method simplifies dicing but requires an extra glass transfer step, while the faced-down method avoids glass transfer step but increases the risk of chipping and cracks. Tape and blade selection are crucial. By using low-adhesion ultraviolet (UV) curable tapes avoids residue and resin blades offering ultra smooth dicing performance compared to metal blade. By optimizing cutting parameters through design of experiments (DOE), chipping size is controlled and a process capability index (Cpk) greater than 1.67 is achieved.

articleTitle: Breakthrough Bundle X-out Fiducial Design for Multi-up PCB
abstract: There are few methods to manage the panel with X-out board for board manufacturing. One of the methods is to black marked the fiducial of the individual X-out board so that when the P&P(pick-and-place) equipment’s camera capture the black marked fiducial image, it will skip the X-out board for component placement. Same concept work for AOI machine to skip the X-out board for inspection. However, fiducial image capturing for individual board is a time consuming process and it will reduce the output of the board manufacturing significantly. A new approach called ‘Bundle X-out Fiducial’(BXF) has been designed to increase the beat rate of the board manufacturing if compared to the conventional method of individual board fiducial scanning. The idea of the bundle X-out fiducial is to design a group of special fiducials which are close to each other at outrigger of the panel which representing each single board location on the panel. The BXF will reduce the travel time of the P&P equipment’s camera to capture and recognize the X-out fiducial, hence, reduce the P&P cycle time by ~50%. This paper will review the design pattern of the BXF.

articleTitle: Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) Transmitter Preset Coefficient Autotune Algorithm
abstract: Transmitter equalization plays a very important factor in Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe), which could cause bad data transfers in case poor quality of link equalization due to high frequency channel losses. Preset test is one of the electrical compliance tests that must pass in compliance workshop to formally label products as compliant. Currently, the tuning of the presets is done manually by engineers, which is time consuming and might not optimize to reach an ideal set of coefficients. In this paper, autotune process is introduced to predict the most optimized preshoot (PS) and deemphasis (DE) value for those preset that are marginal or not meeting the specification. By using the baseline measurement of PS and DE, the most optimized value based on the ideal calculation of each increment or decrement of PS and DE is predicted and feedbacked to the real measurement to verify. Experimental results show that the sample able to tune to a better optimized PS and DE value, allowing more than 25% margin from the upper and lower limit of specification.

articleTitle: The Effect of Ion Implantation on Carbon Diffusion Through Si/SiOx Layer
abstract: The mechanism of carbon (C) diffusion in Silicon Oxide (SiOx) that is deposited on silicon (Si) wafer through the furnace oxidation process, has been investigated in different pre-conditions (with and without ion implantation & with and without O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> leak during thermal treatment). The diffusive behaviour of C through SiOx was monitored by X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS). The C in SiOx on ion-implanted Si wafer is 6.04 at% at & 2.4 at% for bulk & interlayer respectively. While under O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> leakage condition during thermal treatment, the concentration of C is 0.63 at% and 0.8 at% in the upper and lower part of the SiOx bulk layer respectively. However, the concentration of C in SiOx on ion implantation-free Si wafers are 7.54 at% and 6.0 at% for bulk & interlayer respectively. Under O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> leakage conditions during thermal treatment, the C concentration of ion implantation-free wafer is also relatively high at 2.14 at% and 1.89 at% for upper & lower SiOx bulk respectively. The C diffusion profiles show that ion-implanted Si wafers have lower C impurities due to faster out-diffusion of C from the Si substrate in both O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> leaked & and O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> leaked conditions during thermal treatment. On the other hand, ion implantation-free Si wafer has higher C impurities due to slower out-diffusion of C. This suggested that the implantation process can cause certain damage on the Si wafer surface, leading to faster out-diffusion of C during the thermal treatment step.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fault Localization strategies through versatile Sample Preparation Techniques for Electro Migration defect preservation and characterization
abstract: This paper presents a cutting-edge extension of the package-die level sample preparation approach that allows for a versatile fault localization step in identifying the electromigration signature (EM) in power-integrated circuits that utilize Copper Redistribution Layer (CuRDL) technology. This innovative methodology demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of the nature of the defect by manipulating well-known failure analysis (FA) methods to pinpoint the exact location where the defect resides. The process consists of backside sample preparation, followed by fault localization using the Optical Beam Induced Resistance Change (IR-Obirch) method. Then, it continues with the newly introduced package lapping method from the frontside under controlled conditions. The analysis further characterizes the defect using advanced cross-sectional analysis techniques, including Focused Ion Beam (FIB) and Energy Dispersive X-ray (EDX), which are widely employed in semiconductor analysis. As a result, the signature of the copper element, which had already blended, was identified, and suggested the mechanism of its migration from the anode terminal toward the cathode terminal in the metal interconnection layer. The failure mechanism suggested signs of penetration through the photosensitive layer, which finally resulted in electrical breakdown and severely impacted the area. Based on the achieved results, by leveraging a combination of FA techniques, analysts were able to gain a deeper understanding of the root cause of the defect and can develop targeted solutions to address it.

articleTitle: Energy Saving in Semiconductor Packaging Plating Processes Through Chemical Deflashing Process Optimization
abstract: The growing emphasis on sustainable manufacturing processes and corporate social responsibility has led to increased interest in utilizing environmentally or eco-friendly and green chemicals that offer reduced hazards and greater sustainability. This shift is particularly evident in the exploration of alternatives to traditional chemical dipping deflashing processes used to eliminate excessive mold bleed resulting from molding operations. Assessment of excessive flashes typically relies on visual inspection and considers the impact of delamination on the leadframe to the mold compound interface. Conventionally, these processes utilize high-temperature, low flash point, water-soluble solvents, despite their drawbacks, including the generation of hazardous fumes and substantial electrical power demands for temperature control. This study delves into the feasibility of using lower temperature and no flash point chemicals to achieve comparable deflashing effectiveness without inducing delamination between the leadframe and mold compound. The findings reveal the potential to reduce chemical temperatures by up to 40 percent while still achieving effective deflashing results. This reduction in temperature not only mitigates the production of hazardous fumes but also diminishes the power requirements for heating during the deflashing process, thereby fostering a safer working environment. The adoption of such eco-friendly chemicals in deflashing processes aligns with broader sustainability objectives and corporate responsibility initiatives, offering both environmental benefits and improvements in operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Effective Lead Lock Tape Solution for Mitigating Leadframe's Lead Bend in Semiconductor Packaging
abstract: The relentless drive for miniaturization in semiconductor packaging has led to thinner and narrower leads, making them vulnerable to inner lead bending during the assembly process or handling. This issue presents a significant obstacle for semiconductor manufacturers, affecting product reliability and resulting in high rework costs.
