To address this challenge, an effective solution has been proposed: lead lock tape (LLT). The lead lock tape securely immobilizes each lead, creating a physical barrier that prevents adjacent leads from touching or bending during the assembly process or handling. Rigorous experimentation and analysis demonstrate the effectiveness of lead lock tape in mitigating inner lead bending. The experiments cover various package configurations and testing scenarios, closely simulating real-world conditions. Results indicate a substantial reduction in inner lead bending incidents with the application of lead lock tape, enhancing package reliability and reducing manufacturing expenses. Importantly, this solution does not compromise the electrical performance or mechanical integrity of the semiconductor package. Adopting lead lock tape provides a practical and cost-effective strategy to address the persistent challenge of inner lead bending in modern semiconductor packaging. Manufacturers can implement this innovative approach to elevate product reliability, streamline production processes, and meet the demands of intricate electronic devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing AOI with AI for Printed Circuit Board Assembly – A Comprehensive Industry Study
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) systems holds significant potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of defect detection in Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA). This paper presents the findings of an industry-wide study conducted by the International Electronics Manufacturing Initiative (iNEMI) on the adoption and enhancement of AI in AOI systems. Building on the results of Phase 1, which established performance metrics and identified key challenges, Phase 2 involved experimental evaluations to provide industry-wide recommendations. The study highlights the benefits, challenges, and future directions for AI-enhanced AOI systems.

articleTitle: C5 Reflow and Flux Clean Characterization for Automotive FCBGA
abstract: This study focused on C5 leadfree solder reflow and flux clean characterization on FCBGA for automotive application. Impact of short versus long time above solder liquidus temperature (TAL) on intermetallic growth, solder ball shear strength and fracture mode were studied. A very short TAL resulted in higher solder ball shear strength and near to zero intermetallic layer formation. A very long TAL had significant thicker intermetallic growth and low shear strength. A balance TAL within flux-solder reflow profile recommendation was employed to overcome the 2 TAL extremes of poor joint and thick intermetallic layer. DI water flux clean interaction between different water pressure zones and spray type were studied. Change in wash zone water pressure impacts the pre-wash zone water pressure. Top piping pressure in each zone were set to maximum to ensure continuous water flooding on BGA side of all units while bottom piping pressure were set to values that prevented unit fly off. Spray type water reach was studied to ensure all units received water spray consistently. Drying zone temperature and conveyor speed were studied and successfully determined to ensure units received temperature above water boiling point for complete unit drying.

articleTitle: Multi Row QFN Wire Gap Clearance Improvement Using Improved Mold Compound
abstract: The Multi row quad flat no lead (MRQFN) package is known to be a low-cost package that offers high pin count similar to the ball grid array (BGA) package [1]. Augmented with exposed pad, it can offer both improved thermal dissipation and electrical grounding effect, rendering it suitable for compact design in high-power and high-frequency applications including both automotive and non-automotive products. In many occasions, due to intricate wire layout, multi-tiered wire bond looping and long wire span are required. Hence, the primary challenge is to optimize wire gap clearance to prevent wire short after molding, and any latent reliability failure such as leakage due to inadequate wire gap. To achieve optimal wire gap, the crucial factors to be considered are like wire configuration, wire location, bond pad pitch, mold gate design and mold flow direction. In addition, epoxy molding compound (EMC) properties particularly mold spiral flow is also equally important, which will affect the mold flow during transfer molding. In this paper, the importance of longer spiral flow in EMC was studied in detailed, underscoring its role and characterizing its viscosity behavior. In summary, through a series of wire gap improvements by wire loop profile and molding process optimization, a remarkable improvement in term of wire gap clearance and wire sweep performance were achieved, particularly for wires at die corners. Wire gap post molding of more than 2x wire diameter was accomplished while wire sweep was reduced to less than 10%. The final solution also passed electrical test after temperature cycle (TC) and biased high accelerated stress test (HAST) that proved the effectiveness of the solution

articleTitle: Exploring the Correlation Between Post-Die Bond Epoxy Void and Bond Line Thickness and other Factors on Power Packaging with Silver Sintered Epoxy
abstract: As 5th Generation (5G) deployments continue to expand globally, network operators need to extend their coverage while maintaining performance. The extension of 5G coverage requires wide-bandgap semiconductors such as GaN, GaAs, and SiC chip technology on power products such as PDFN(Power Dual No-lead). The packaging requirement also increases in term of high thermal dissipation ability under high temperature power devices conditions. Selection of die attach material with higher thermal conductivity and establish its process control is crucial in development of PDFN package for 5G application. This study diverges from conventional conductive epoxies, opting for Agsintered epoxy with a leadframe characterized by higher thermal and electrical conductivity. The research examines die bonding characteristics, aiming to identify crucial factors contributing to minimizing Ag sintered epoxy voids which could potentially compromise device performance especially in scenarios involving multiple die configurations and Ag-plated leadframe finish. The study focuses on characterization of bond line thickness (BLT) of Ag-sintered epoxy with different material properties through series of Design of Experiment (DOE) and establish correlation between epoxy void and BLT. The study also include other factors that influence the epoxy void such as die back metal type, height bonding, and force bonding concepts. The investigation provides essential insights into improving the die attach process by reducing epoxy voids across diverse conditions, offering invaluable guidance for semiconductor packaging processes. The findings, highly relevant in the ever-changing landscape of 5G technologies, tackle challenges related to coverage expansion and device performance optimization.

articleTitle: Micro bumping via Paste Dispensing Technology for Advanced Packaging
abstract: Solder paste dispensing technology has been widely used in the semiconductor industry for many years for die attach application. The industry is driving towards a complex design for advance packaging, with component design layout with smaller footprints. Traditional stencil printing cannot be applied to certain packaging designs, particularly those with irregular substrates or space limitations. Therefore, dispensing is a suitable alternative method. Ultra-fine solder paste for dispensing (≥80 µm) is only achievable with the correct combination of paste formulation and dispensing equipment. Solder pastes with consistent powder size distribution and spherical finer powder shape is needed to dispense a finer dot of ≥80 µm. Type 6 powders processed by Welco technology have a tight powder size distribution and are highly spherical. Solder paste made with this powder and a water-soluble flux platform provide consistent dispensing volume, while eliminating the needle clogging and missing dots issue. Time pressure and squeeze pump dispensing methods for solder paste application were validated. This paper will discuss the paste formulation and dispensing equipment’s contribution to enable dispensing of dot size ≥80 µm.(a)Time pressure dispensing method evaluated and dot size achieved 200-250 µm without defects.(b)Squeezing dispensing method evaluated, successfully dispensed dot size 80-100 µm without significant defects such as missing and inconsistent dots.

articleTitle: Novel Bond-Wire Optimization Method for PISI and Yield Improvement
abstract: With technology shrinking and increasing device functionality, device power and performance imposes major challenges to meet overall system level electrical specification. These electrical specifications such as PISI, EMI/EMC, IR Drop, PDN Impedance, I/O interface timing, BOM cost etc. play important part in Die-PKG-PCB Co-design for complex SoC having high-speed interfaces designed for different applications. In this paper, we propose a novel bond-wire optimization method in the wire-bond package to reduce Power-Ground (PG) pins. Reducing PG pins can provide more signal pins for customer application and reduce PG pads at die level to optimize die size for complex SoC having high-speed interfaces to meet overall electrical specifications and yield. PG pads at die are connected to PG ring/bar and ground flag which are connected to package pins. Bond-wire connected from isolated ring to package pin is called jumper wires. These jumper wires are required to reduce package parasitics (Resistance (R), Inductance (L) and Capacitance (C) to meet electrical specification. However, jumper wire bonding can impose manufacturing challenges during assembly. An example was seen with a high volume manufacturing product which has high package yield loss (~1000ppm). In this paper, jumper bond-wire optimization with an evaluation vehicle is presented to improve the package yield loss and at the same time meeting the overall system level electrical specifications for the complex SoC.

articleTitle: Auto Phase Management Optimization of Multiphase Voltage Regulator to Improve ErP Lot 3 Performance Per Watt
abstract: The paper introduces auto phase management (APM) as a means to enhance power delivery efficiency in computers, aiming to achieve higher Performance per Watt (PPW) scores under the Energy-related Products (ErP) Lot 3 regulations set by the European Commission. The latest version of the Personal Computer Energy Efficiency Tool evaluates PPW by executing a set of 18 benchmark software (worklets) on the unit under test (UUT). Subsequently, the European Commission plans to categorize UUT scores into 7 energy classes for all computers sold in the European Union. Improving PPW can be achieved by either enhancing performance at constant power or maintaining performance while reducing power consumption.This paper focuses on the introduction of APM and its role in enhancing power delivery efficiency, leading to improved PPW scores in compliance with ErP Lot 3 regulations. It discusses the design considerations of APM, its correlation with ErP Lot 3 worklets' current and residency data and presents APM test results. Through this exploration, the paper aims to provide insights into how APM can be leveraged to optimize computer energy efficiency and meet regulatory standards effectively.

articleTitle: Illuminating Precision: Enhancing Clip Attach Vision Accuracy in Semiconductor Manufacturing
abstract: In the global technology landscape, the outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) sector is pivotal for assembling, testing, and packaging electronic devices. Quality maintenance within OSAT operations directly influences product performance, reliability, and lifespan. This study addressed a significant quality issue in semiconductor manufacturing—clip lifting due to insufficient solder paste on the wafer die surface—which leads to increased lot rejection rates and manufacturing inefficiencies. To resolve this issue, the Six Sigma methodology, specifically the Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control (DMAIC) approach, was employed. This structured framework facilitated problem-solving and process improvement. By mitigating clip lifting, the study aimed to reduce rework costs, enhance customer satisfaction, and build confidence in manufacturing processes. This project successfully reduced clip lifting defects from an average defect rate of 5.6% to below the targeted baseline of 2.6%. Statistical analytical tools such as chi-square testing were used to confirm the impact of vision detection settings on defect occurrence. An optimized solder paste detection vision brightness level was determined as an improvement to overcome occurrence of less solder dispense on die surface. This systematic approach demonstrated effective problem solving and process optimization, contributing to broader quality enhancement in the semiconductor industry.

articleTitle: Fluorine Residue Reduction in Plasma Dicing
abstract: This paper showcases an innovative characterization in reducing fluorine residue in the plasma dicing process applied to RFID application wafers. The advantages of plasma dicing include a reduction in sawlane width, leading to an increase in Die Counts per Wafer (DPW) and enhanced die strength. This is achieved through a chemical etching process that separates the silicon wafer dies. The requirement for small die sizes in RFID applications results in a high DPW, exceeding 300,000 on a single wafer, and a narrower sawlane of less than 10um. Consequently, a plasma dicing solution becomes essential for RFID wafers. The Reactive Ion Etching (RIE) plasma dicing process, also known in the industry as Bosch Process is a high aspect ratio plasma etching process. This process provides a protective fluorocarbon layer on the sidewall for an anisotropic fluorine-based etching process. However, a challenge arises as the fluorinated gas used in plasma dicing can induce contamination on the sidewall or surface of the wafer. This contamination may affect the adhesion between the die and the backgrind tape. Particularly for small RFID dies on the wafer edge that need to adhere to the lamination tape post-backgrinding, the adhesion force can be compromised when fluorine contamination occurs at the wafer edge. This study was conducted to creatively optimize the RIE polymerization process and the fluorine residue cleaning process post-plasma dicing. The results of the study were analyzed using SEM and XPS tools to determine the level of fluorine residue. The analysis indicates a significant reduction in fluorinated material, demonstrating a positive outcome, hence making this study a success.

articleTitle: Effect Of Anti-Epoxy Bleed Out Concentration And Leadframe Plating Condition Towards Die Attach Glue Bleed Out Performance
abstract: This technical paper is entitled "Effect of Anti-Glue Bleed Out (Anti-EBO) concentration and leadframe (LF) plating condition towards Die Attach glue bleed out performance". One of the main challenges faced by Die Attach (DA) process assembly manufacturing is glue bleed out (EBO). EBO is a phenomenon whereby there is separation of some formulation ingredients in the paste from its bulk paste, either reactive diluents, resins, catalysts, or additives, wetting leadframe surfaces adjacent to the die paddle area. As counter measure for EBO, leadframe surface will be treated and coated with anti-EBO solutions to prevent and control the resin from flowing into the leadframe and causing cosmetic and reliability issue. This technical paper aims to provide a better perspective in multiple factors that can affect glue bleed out during Die Attach process, such as anti EBO concentration and plating conditions and parameters used during lead frame manufacturing. The study was conducted by varying the concentration of anti-EBO coating applied to the leadframe surface, water rinse pump used, rinsing method, and dryer temperature of the leadframe. As response, the EBO performance was evaluated through visual inspection and measurement of glue bleed out spread. The results showed that the concentration of anti-EBO coating and some of plating conditions during leadframe manufacturing have a significant impact on the performance of glue bleed out. This paper highlights the importance of controlling the concentration of anti-EBO coating and the leadframe plating condition to improve the performance of glue bleed out at Die Attach process.

articleTitle: Development of Panel Level Packaging for Multi-Chip Modules with High-Precision Redistribution Layer
abstract: The swift progression of artificial intelligence, particularly exemplified by the recent advancements in ChatGPT, necessitates markedly increased data transfer rates. Among the advanced packaging techniques, Fan-Out Multi-Chip Module (FOMCM) technology is distinguished by its cost-effectiveness and high-speed data transmission capabilities. FOMCM manufacturing is produced at the wafer level for sizes up to 12 inches (300 mm). To further enhance productivity and reduce costs, the transition to larger form factors is under investigation. The panel dimensions considered in this shift range from 300x300 mm to 510x515 mm, and potentially up to 600x600 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.This paper demonstrates the development of a Chiplet package using panel-level FOMCM technology. The designed package has dimensions of 65x65 mm and includes four integrated dies. These dies are mounted onto three pre-fabricated redistribution layers (RDLs) using the Flip-chip (FC) technique, executed on a glass panel measuring 510x515 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Furthermore, this study addresses the primary challenges encountered in panel-level packaging (PLP), such as warpage, and die shift, and provides insights into overcoming these obstacles.

articleTitle: Investigating Crystallography and Thickness Distribution of Aluminium Nitride Thin Films Prepared by Magnetron Sputtering on Silicon Wafer
abstract: This study utilized radio frequency magnetron sputtering to deposit aluminum nitride (AlN) thin film onto a silicon wafer at room temperature. The investigation focused on characterizing the thin film's crystal structure and thickness distribution across different positions within a 4-inch wafer area, utilizing both static and rotated substrate holders. Generally, the X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectrum shows three main crystal planes of (100), (002), and (101) that belong to AlN. Static holder conditions exhibited significant variations among crystal planes, indicating non-homogeneous deposition. Particularly, a strong (002) peak was determined near the target source, as expected due to the plasma concentration and higher energy of sputtering particles directed toward the substrate at that specific position. On the other hand, rotated holders produced nearly identical spectra but with weaker peaks due to shadowing and stagnation effects. Deposition angle and particle energy impacted crystal orientation and XRD peak intensities. The standard deviation for thickness was 43.22 nm with static holders, reduced to 19.45 nm with rotated holders, showing uniform thickness distribution with minimal variation across different positions. This research aids in understanding large-area thin film deposition, particularly for AlN templates in microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) applications and as buffer layers for gallium nitride (GaN) devices.

articleTitle: High-Density Flip Chip Solder Bump Bridging Detection Using YOLOv7
abstract: Solder bump bridging (SBB) induced during chip attach process could cause electrical failure and device to malfunction. These SBB defects went undetected due to complex circuitry, test detectability and coverage. This paper focuses on AI development using YOLOv7 to improve SBB detectability in manufacturing assembly. We’ve implemented an image quality and alignment check algorithm, augmented the images, tuned the hyperparameters and trained an SBB defect detection model. Our model can generalize across multiple datasets achieving a recall score above 0.97. The experimental results show that our proposed method is effective in detecting solder bumps bridging defects.

articleTitle: Voiding Control of Lead-Free Soldering at Quad-flat No-lead package Components
abstract: the quad-flat no-lead (QFN) package design is widely applied in many new applications due to benefits including small size, reduced lead inductance, and good thermal and electrical performance. However, it remains challenging to control thermal pad voiding under QFN due to the large coverage area and low standoff. Many parameters, such as solder paste flux type, powder size, powder quality, surface finish, and component size can impact voiding behavior. In addition, process parameters such as stencil design, printing, and reflow also have a strong impact on voiding. In this work, reflow profile, reflow atmosphere, solder particle size for different type of solder paste flux on organic solderability preservative (OSP) substrate were evaluated. Results of investigation indicate that void was decreased with increasing temperature above liquidus (TAL) and peak temperature. Solder paste flux type effects were strong and reflow atmosphere effects were moderate for 96.5Sn3.0Ag0.5Cu (SAC305) Type 4 powder, both of which increased for SAC305 Type 5 powder.

articleTitle: Developing a Simulation Model to Improve Strip Warpage Performance Predictability
abstract: Encapsulation is a process for protecting Die and Wire with protective material EMC. Elevated temperatures after the Post Encapsulation process may cause package warping—deviate from an ideal state of uniform planar flatness, commonly referred to as warpage/coplanarity. Actual warpage measurement only able to know after FUT (Functional Unit Test), and if value is more than specification of package design, it needs to be yield off and will have huge impacts on the entire development process in terms of cost and time to market. With improved technology, market needs for thinner die will be more prominent, and then the problems related to warpage will also be substantial. In such scenarios, having an algorithm or model that predicts strip warpage performance before FUT will be beneficial and can be mitigated earlier in the line. Hence, in this paper, we have used the bi-layer cantilever beam model (2D model) to predict the package warpage. We optimized, validated, and correlated it w.r.t. our data in order to stimulate the actual warpage performance of the package. Through advanced modelling techniques of MATLAB and SIMULINK, the research dwells on the major factors impacting warpage performance and hence seeks to enhance their predictability toward improving package designing.

articleTitle: An Innovative Hybrid Cleaning Approach for Contaminant Removal in Semiconductor Packaging
abstract: Delamination poses a significant challenge in semiconductor industry, particularly in electric vehicle (EV) components, impacting their performance and reliability. It occurs when the adhesion between the encapsulation material and the leadframe fails, often due to thermal stress. Roughened leadframes have been adopted to enhance their interlocking among them. However, this approach inadvertently introduces surface contamination during flux cleaning, which can compromise wire bonding quality. The presence of such contamination underscores the need for more sophisticated cleaning methods. This study investigates a hybrid cleaning solution designed to reduce surface contamination on roughened leadframes. Conventional immersion-type cleaning has shown limitations in effectively addressing this issue. Therefore, a hybrid method combining immersion-type flux cleaning with subsequent spray-in-air cleaning process using deionized (DI) water is proposed. This dual approach leverages the advantages of both immersion and high-pressure DI water spray, improving cleaning efficiency and minimizing contamination. Extensive testing under various conditions has demonstrated a marked reduction in surface contamination compared to conventional methods, significantly lowering the risk of defects such as non-stick on lead (NSOL) or non-stick on pad (NSOP). The paper discusses the mechanism behind this hybrid cleaning approach, offering a pathway forward for optimizing flux cleaning on roughened leadframes and enhancing overall wire bonding reliability.

articleTitle: Exploring the Patent Landscape of Sintered Metal Technologies: An Analysis Using LLM-Based AI Patent Search
abstract: This study leveraged a proprietary Large Language Model (LLM) via app.amplified.ai, focusing on sintered metal technology patents for die-bonding uses in electronics packaging. This AI platform analyzed patent complexities, particularly examining 11 pre-selected patents with known activities on uses of silver or copper paste formulations as die-attach materials from companies like Infineon Technologies, Siemens, Nihon Superior Tanaka Kikinzoku, Heraeus, Hitachi and Alphametals. Following similarity assessments with these 11 pre-selected patents, 243 core patents were identified from the app.amplified.ai patent databases (of more than 150 million), retrieved and analyzed, resulting in six key clusters: 1) conductive adhesive bonding 2) metal particle bonding 3) porous metal bonding 4) sintered silver bonding, 5) substrate bonding methods 6) terminal management bonding. These clusters match the dominant Cooperative Patent Cooperation codes as follows: H01L24/83, H01L24/29 and H01L2224/8384; all methods related to connecting semiconductor using layer connector, and mainly with sintering technology. Finally, these clusters helped to outline the interconnections among patents, their legal statuses, and assignees from 1994 to 2024, offering valuable insights for patent analytics regarding significant patents and the main technology players for this sintered bonding

articleTitle: Die Cost Reduction Through Re-architecting Power Delivery Network Design and Enabling Common Package Footprint
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to achieve die cost reduction while enabling multiple innovative power delivery network (PDN) design techniques to preserve a common package footprint, which allows ‘one shot 2 kills’ savings for this project. A few significant challenges addressed in this study is the lowering of Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) Capacitance density, enabling the development of a solution with >4x lower MIM density at lower die cost. To address the complexities arising from MIMCAP reduction, an iterative methodology is employed to assess and mitigate power supply noise and cross-coupling effects in a disaggregated architecture. Feature enhancements such as improved noise isolation, optimized MIMCAP distribution, and adaptive PDN configurations are introduced to ensure robust performance under evolving market demands. The outcome of this research demonstrates that innovative PDN re-architecting can maintain power integrity (PI) performance within a negligible 5% delta.

articleTitle: Investigation of PMOS Transistor Threshold Voltage Shift in BCD Technology
abstract: A new failure mechanism of P-channel metal oxide semiconductor (PMOS) transistor threshold voltage (Vth) shift due to unintentional N-type doping onto silicon wafer from wafer fab environment, which occurred after Nanospray wet cleaning and just before oxidation, was investigated. Electrical Failure Analysis (EFA) was used to provide a reasonable explanation for the PMOS Vth shift. The doping profile of the affected PMOS transistor was successfully derived from Capacitance-Voltage (C-V) measurement, which allowed us to compare the silicon surface N-type doping concentration below the gate oxide between affected and reference samples. Numerous experiments were conducted to gather evidence supporting the hypothesis that unintentional N-type doping, transported from wafer fab environment onto the silicon wafer, causes the observed Vth shift. We implemented an effective corrective action to eliminate the risk of Vth shift, by removing affected wet cleaning process right before oxidation from affected process routes.

articleTitle: Synergistic Interactions Between Water-Soluble Solder Paste and Ultrasonic Flux Cleaning in Producing Zero Solder Ball Rejects
abstract: The semiconductor packaging industry is growing rapidly driven, in part, by the booming sales of high-performance electric vehicles with advanced Internet of Things (IoT) features. As a result, the reliability requirements for the packages are getting more and more stringent. In common solder paste die attach applications, the presence of solder balls is often a roadblock to the reliability performance of the packages. Optimizing the reflow profile is the typical and straightforward approach to minimize the chances of solder ball formations by adjusting parameters such as the temperature ramp rates and peak temperatures. Nevertheless, getting the optimized parameters is very challenging and time consuming due to the necessity for extensive experimentations. Yet, this approach is still unable to ensure zero solder ball rejects. In this study, a robust solution is proposed to remove the solder balls completely. This solution utilizes the synergistic interactions between water-soluble solder pastes and ultrasonic flux cleaning as the mechanism to remove the solder balls effectively. In addition, the proposed solution is deemed to be applicable to other packages with solder paste die attach.

articleTitle: Effect of Lead Lock Tape Mirror tool (LLT) towards machine performance & yield
abstract: This technical paper title is "Effect of Lead Lock Tape (LLT) Mirror-like surface parts towards machine performance & yield." One of the critical challenges faced by LLT process is the tape residue formation. Tape residue formation is a defect whereby there is an excess tape adhesive film that falls and sticks on the frame (falling material) due to abrasion between tape and parts surface during the lead lock tape punching process. As corrective action for tape residue formation, the part surface for the LLT process must be in mirror condition which reduces the abrasion effect between the tape edges and tool’s punch and die surface. This technical paper aims to provide better perspective in LLT parts mirror-like surface condition that can affect the machine performance & yield. The study was conducted by varying roughness, Ra value of the LLT part’s surface. As response, the machine performance & yield is evaluated by the LLT machine automated visual inspection (AVI) & lead frame automated optical inspection (AOI). The outcome shows that the mirror-like condition of the tool’s parts plays a vital role in the machine performance & process yield. This paper focuses on the importance of controlling mirror-like tool’s parts condition to improve the machine performance & process yield of LLT process.

articleTitle: Compute Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) Silicon Spacer Elimination - A Process Simplification Approach
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to improve the efficiency of Compute DRAM packaging in the PCB industry. The current process involves the use of silicon spacers to fill defective boards, a process that consumes significant machine capacity and complicates the process. The paper introduces a unique heater block and window clamp design that eliminates the need for silicon spacers. The new design, rigorously tested, ensures good quality bonding and prevents energy losses. It also avoids potential abrasion and mechanical damage to the die backside, a challenge present in the previous design. The paper further discusses the testing methodology and results, demonstrating comparable performance with the standard setup in terms of wire pull, stitch pull, and bond shear. Assembly and test yields show no significant difference between the new design and the baseline performance. The paper concludes that the new design, passing all reliability tests, successfully simplifies the Compute DRAM packaging process without compromising quality, thereby meeting the increasing demand for memory and storage in today's industry. This innovative approach has the potential to significantly enhance manufacturing efficiency in the PCB industry.

articleTitle: Recent iNEMI Research on Electromigration in Tin-Bismuth Solder
abstract: Near-eutectic tin-bismuth alloy is a strong contender as the solder of choice for low-temperature electronic assembly applications. This paper will describe the recent significant developments by the iNEMI project team on the understanding of the electromigration behavior of Sn-Bi solder which has a unique physical metallurgy and electromigration behavior quite different for that of Sn-Ag-Cu (SAC) solder and other solders in common use today. The high rate of Bi electromigration and its high homologous temperature sets the near-eutectic Sn-Bi solder apart from the SAC and the Sn-Pb solders. The latter have lower homologous temperatures and have no one element dominating the electromigration phenomenon that can be readily tracked to monitor their electromigration behavior. In Sn-Bi alloys, the rates of Bi electromigration are clearly reflected in the rates of electrical resistance increase making it more convenient to use the fundamental physics-based electromigration equations rather than Black’s somewhat empirical equation that deals with the mean time to failure of solder joints. The high homologous temperature of Sn-Bi alloys makes in-situ study of electromigration in a scanning electron microscope more convenient, resulting in a much deeper understanding of the physical metallurgy and electromigration of the Sn-Bi alloys. For example, recent in-situ studies have shown that the root cause of decreasing solder electrical resistance in the early stage of electromigration, very evident at low temperatures and low current densities, is due to the microstructural coarsening of the alloy. When results are summarized on Arrhenius plots, the prediction of electromigration life under any given field condition becomes straightforward.

articleTitle: Pushing the limits of miniaturization in microelectronic packaging via the application of ultra-thin micro dam structures
abstract: The ever-increasing demand for miniaturization in semiconductor and microelectronic packaging is pushing the limits of what is feasible. On the design side, limitations such as space for keep-out zones (e.g. space for the fillet or the dispensing area of an underfill) and the potential flow of encapsulation compounds should not be overlooked in order to avoid contamination of surrounding components. In addition, optical barriers in sensors can often only be achieved using mold structures or by placing barriers (e.g. caps). It is generally preferred that these barriers are narrower and flatter, but this is often limited due to manufacturing reasons.With line widths of 100 µm and less combined with aspect ratios of above 5, DELO Industrial Adhesives, in cooperation with micro dispensing equipment manufacturer NSW Automation, has succeeded in developing a micro dam that creates new possibilities in the field of heterogeneous integration and optical packaging.High dispensing speeds and curing via UV light or heat also make the application process more flexible. Almost limitless designs of free-form structures are thus now possible and completely new package designs can be realized.

articleTitle: Rheological Characterisation of Graphene filled Isotropic Conductive Adhesives
abstract: Isotropic Conductive Adhesives (ICAs) offer a viable alternative to traditional tin/lead soldering methods, which are restricted by regulations such as the European Union’s Restriction of Hazardous Substances Directive (RoHS). The synthesis of graphene oxide (GO) was carried out through Huang's method, followed by reduction using hydrazine as per Stankovich's approach, resulting in reduced graphene oxide (RGO) that accumulated into a solid aggregate. The synthesized RGO particles were manually dispersed in DGEBA epoxy resin and subjected to rheological flow and oscillatory tests using an Anton Paar MCR301 rheometer. The rheological tests revealed that neat (unmixed) epoxy behaves as a Newtonian fluid, while the addition of RGO fillers from 1 to 4 by weight percentage (%) increases viscosity due to particle interference with the flow. Higher filler concentrations, particularly at 4%, resulted in more significant changes, indicating that the rheological properties are strongly influenced by filler content and distribution. In contrast, the graphite sample showed minimal viscosity change due to smoother flow, underscoring the impact of particle shape and alignment on fluid behaviour. The liquid matrix was found to be very stable and resistant to shear-induced destruction, exhibiting Newtonian-like behaviour at filler loadings below 4% by weight. However, at a 4% loading, the material displayed a stepwise rheological transformation, characterized by strong thixotropic behaviour.

articleTitle: A Journey of Bringing Portability to Desktop AIO PC: The Experience & Key Learning
abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic has necessitated a shift towards online work and learning, creating a demand for computing devices that balance mobility with performance and screen size. Addressing this need, a team from Intel Malaysia with funding from the Malaysia Design Center Innovation Fund developed a Proof of Concept (POC) called Alma City. This innovative Thin Mobile All-In-One (AIO) desktop PC prototype combines the benefits of a large screen and high computing power with the convenience of portability within the home. Alma City features a 21.6" 4K OLED display, an 12th Gen Intel® Core™ Processor mobile CPU, an Intel Arc GPUs (codenamed "Alchemist"), and a 36 Whr battery pack. Despite its impressive capabilities, the device is only 11.4 mm thick, weighs under 3 kg, and includes a strap for easy carrying, allowing users to move it around the house as needed. The rubber feet double as strap holders, enhancing its portability. This system is designed to redefine the AIO desktop PC form factor, offering a solution for users who need to transition between workspaces at home without interrupting their tasks, such as video editing. This Portable AIO represents a significant step in meeting the evolving demands for computing devices in a post-pandemic world.

articleTitle: An Innovative Approach to Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (SAM) for Layered Structures in Wafer Level Chip Scale Package (WLCSP)
abstract: This technical paper introduces an innovative approach aimed at overcoming the limitations associated with conventional Scanning Acoustic Microscopy (SAM) techniques in the analysis of Wafer Level Chip Scale Packages (WLCSP). Conventional SAM methods have struggled to fully characterize interfaces within these packages, requiring complex setups with multiple frequency transducers and resulting in limited scanning, especially for Printed-Circuit-Board (PCB) mounted units. A new method to apply 200 MHz UHF (Ultra-High Frequency) transducer for single scanning of multiple layers for both loosen and PCB mounted units are presented in this work. There is currently technique performs a single scan from top to bottom to capture many layers of interfaces in stacked materials. This approach facilitates comprehensive data acquisition across all layers within the WLCSP, especially for PCB mounted. By acquiring information of material factors for specific layers following the properties to derive acoustic impedance, the phase inversion of waveforms can be obtained. Subsequently, step to estimate the gate location is performed on the corresponding interface of interest. Repetitive analysis on SAM and comparative analysis on cross section is carried out to ensure the gate location is positioned accurately between boundary of each material interface. Through rigorous comparative analysis with conventional methods, the outcome of this work demonstrates superior time efficiency while maintaining data integrity and ensuring comprehensive coverage for WLCSP. This proposed technique is expected to overcome the limitations of conventional approaches employed for scanning layered structures in WLCSP.

articleTitle: +Architecting for the first Low Power Double Data Rate 5 (LPDDR5) Memory Module
abstract: Low Power Compression Attached Memory Module 2 (LPCAMM2) is the first LPDDR memory module using Compressive Mounting technology which permits 60% less space on the motherboard, increases performance by 50% and energy efficiency by up to 70% compared to SODIMM. Intel partnering will Dell, has led the development of the module where, through JEDEC, they aligned with OEMs and module developers to carry out the first designs. Understanding the physical constraints of 2x SODIMM, efforts were made to architect the module's design to allow smooth technology transition towards LPCAMM2 without affecting existing laptop platform solutions. Work was done on defining the module size resulting in 78 mm x 23 mm with a 10-layer type-4 1.2 mm thick 2x2+ PCB that houses four LPDDR5 x32 SDRAM, and power delivery solutions. The top layer is used to place the SDRAM and power solution, the inner layers are used for memory and power routing. This solution supports 2-channel, 2-rank, byte mode support, 32 Gb density, and up to 9.6 GT/s bus speed in addition to new P5200 PMIC technology which features DVFSC/DVFSQ low power modes, register security, and overclocking. This paper will discuss in detail on LPCAMM2 attributes, and pathfinding work from the architecture phase to its realization into the market.

articleTitle: Determining Organic Solvent Bath Lifespan in Lead-Frame Cleaning
abstract: In high-power discrete packages, high-lead solder paste is used as the interconnect material between the die and the copper lead frame or copper clips. Flux, a component of high-lead solder paste, aids the soldering process by removing oxidized metal from the surface of the solder alloy and the lead frame. After reflow soldering, cleaning is essential to remove flux residues from high-power discrete packages. This typically involves using an organic solvent in a semi-aqueous cleaning process. The bath lifespan of the organic solvent is a key factor influencing process costs and product quality. Factors such as flux loading, copper content, and water content in the organic solvent were studied to understand their impact on the bath lifespan in the semi- aqueous centrifugal cleaning process. Various evaluation methods were developed using bath monitoring techniques to investigate these factors and assess their impact on bath lifetime. A packaging quality assessment was also performed to ensure that the determined bath life does not affect package quality. The findings were correlated with several customer case studies to validate the results and determine the organic solvent bath life in lead frame defluxing processes using a centrifugal cleaning system.

articleTitle: Impact of Thermomechanical Fatigue and Creep on the Reliability of BGA Lead-Free Solder Joints in Electronic Modules
abstract: Ball grid array (BGA) packages, crucial in modern electronics, have significant potential to promote sustainable manufacturing. However, the reliability of BGAs using lead-free tin-silver-copper (SAC) solder alloys needs full qualification, particularly for mission-critical applications. This study examines the thermomechanical fatigue and creep responses of Sn63Pb37, SAC305, SAC387, SAC396, and SAC405 solder joints in BGA packages under thermal cycling, using finite element analysis (FEA) with Garofalo’s hyperbolic sine law for solder material behavior. SAC387 and SAC405 alloys exhibited promising properties, making them strong candidates as alternatives to the traditional Sn63Pb37 solder. As per the results, SAC387 demonstrated the greatest stiffness and resistance to elastic deformation, though it showed a higher susceptibility to creep compared to other alloys. SAC405 emerged as the most durable, exhibiting minimal plastic deformation and strain under thermal stress, making it ideal for resisting failure. The critical areas for crack initiation and propagation were identified at the interfaces between the solder and both the chip and substrate. These findings align with existing research, highlighting key factors in the reliability of solder joints under thermal cycling and creep.

articleTitle: Enhanced Control of WLCSP Wafer Dicing through Big Data Automation and Analysis
abstract: Wafer dicing is a crucial step in the semiconductor industry, particularly with blade sawing leading to small PPM (Parts Per Million) of chip and crack defects. This issue is intensified in Wafer Level Chip Scale Package (WLCSP) devices as die sizes decrease and thicknesses become thinner. Ensuring quality without compromising device shipment requires meticulous control over the wafer dicing process. While Fault Detection Classification (FDC) is a common method for enhanced control, its high setup costs and capital requirements can be prohibitive. This paper proposes a cost-effective alternative, demonstrating the team's approach of automating machine data logs from the wafer dicing machine for monitoring. Control is achieved through statistical analytical techniques, offering a proactive methodology for problem-solving and process improvement. The paper outlines a Proof of Concept with four main steps: automated machine data log, data pre-processing, algorithm investigation and visualization/package solution for ad-hoc analysis. The resulting dashboard facilitates monitoring of key dicing and blade input /output responses, incorporating statistical analyses such as outlier analysis and comparative methods for mean and variance.

articleTitle: High Density Interconnect (HDI) Socket Dynamic Warpage Prediction by Mori-Tanaka Model
abstract: High-density interconnect (HDI) sockets, primarily designed for CPUs and GPUs, are shifting towards larger form factors as the number of interconnect pins increases. The dynamic warpage prediction and control during reflow onto the printed circuit board is the main challenges for large socket. The liquid crystal polymer (LCP) material used in the socket manufacturing exhibited an anisotropic behaviour due to mixture of inherently anisotropic polymer matrix with anisotropic fillers, as compared to general plastics. Socket warpage may under or over predict with standard composite model assumption. This was attributed to the polymer matrix, which was assumed to be a homogeneous material within the composite model. Thus, a new Mori-Tanaka mechanics model was investigated as it has the capabilities to incorporate both polymer matrix and fillers anisotropic effect. A commercial injection molding simulation tool, Moldex3D was employed and validated with experimental measurements. Composite model recorded a larger prediction variation for both room temperature (RT) and high temperature (HT) warpage. In comparison, Mori-Tanaka model predicted better RT and HT comparison, and with good correlation (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>>0.8) obtained. Thus, this studied has demonstrated a new modelling methodology to improve prediction accuracy.
